name: Leadership
about: Practical leadership for people who build with technology and AI: true stories, verified quotes from leaders and management thinkers, and lessons, each with a card designed to match.
crew: Chooses the day's story, quote or lesson.
Searches Wikiquote and the web for leaders' own words.
Proves every quote is real before it is used.
Finds the root cause of a missed post and fixes it within minutes.

name: AI interview question
about: One real question from an AI Architect or AI Developer interview, as a candidate reported it, answered at architect level. The company is named only when the candidate's report names it.
crew: Searches candidates' interview reports from the last year, never question banks or prep portals.
Confirms in code that the question is in the report, word for word.
Explains what is being tested, a strong answer and the common mistakes.
Puts the question on the card.
Rejects an answer that is wrong or too shallow.
Moves to the next topic and finds another question if a run fails.

name: AI news digest
about: The day's top AI updates in one post, every claim traced to its source. The longest-serving team.
crew: Gathers the top ten AI updates and drops repeats.
Drafts the digest in my voice.
Checks every claim against its source and rewrites once if needed.

name: Tech learning
about: Tier lists, comparisons and explainers, researched from the last month's sources.
crew: Chooses the topic and the format.
Finds the root cause of a missed post and fixes it within minutes.

name: Brand analytics
about: Measures how the brand is growing and publishes the numbers on this site, with every figure traceable to its source.
crew: Collects followers, impressions and engagement from LinkedIn, plus every post the workforce made.
Writes the summary; a code check rejects any number that is not in the data.
Updates this site and confirms the new numbers are live.

name: LinkedIn insights
about: Studies what makes public posts on AI and leadership perform, then tells each team what to change. Every claim is checked against the numbers before any team sees it.
crew: Plans the week's searches across six themes, within strict spending limits.
Explains the statistics and the engagement model in plain words.
Turns verified findings into changes for each team; code rejects advice that is not backed by a strong result.

name: Distribution
about: Shares every post on X, Bluesky, Facebook and Dev.to, between 10 and 90 minutes after it goes out on LinkedIn, one platform at a time. The post stays the same; only LinkedIn wording is adjusted.
crew: Picks up each new post with its text and card.
Posts a 300-character version with the card and links to follow.
Publishes the leadership, interview and learning posts as full articles.
Shares the whole post with its card on the TechNaom AI Labs page.
Sends a short version with no links, at most four posts a day.

name: Operations
about: Keeps the whole workforce cheap and healthy, with nobody watching dashboards.
crew: Reports yesterday's spend per workflow and per model every morning.
Compares yesterday with the 28 days before it and raises an alert only when something is far from usual.
Studies every failed run, names the cause with the log lines that prove it, and emails a report.
Makes the smallest code change that fixes a bug the analyst found, and opens a pull request only when every check passes.
Before any fix, writes a test that fails because of the bug, so the fixer has to make it pass without touching it.
A different AI model reads the exact change and approves it only if it removes the cause, not just the symptom.
Releases an approved fix only when every check has passed and no post is due, then keeps it only if the next post publishes.

name: Comment copilot
about: Drafts comments in my own voice on posts in my feed. I choose, edit and post every one myself.
crew: Offers a short, a medium and a long version, never gushing.
